Lemma 3.2. Let M be an R -module. Suppose that I is an ideal of R and N ∈ mod R such that Supp N ⊂ V ( I ) . Then the following assertions hold for any non-negative integer n .

- (1) If Ext i R ( R/I,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n , then Ext i R ( N,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .
- (2) If Tor R i ( R/I,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n , then Tor R i ( N,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .

Since E p,q ∞ is isomorphic to a subquotient of E p,q 2 , we have E p,q ∞ ∈ S for 0 ⩽ q ⩽ n and any p . Hence Ext i R ( R/ p j , M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n . (3.3) Let I = ( x 1 , x 2 , · · · , x n ) be an ideal of R and M a complex of R -modules. In the following, we use K ( I ) to denote the Koszul complex with respect to I = ( x 1 , x 2 , · · · , x n ). The Koszul complex K ( I ) is a bounded complex of finite free modules. Then we define H i ( K ( I ) , M ) := Tor R i ( K ( I ) , M ) = H i ( K ( I ) ⊗ R M ) and H i ( K ( I ) , M ) := Ext i R ( K ( I ) , M ) = H i (Hom R ( K ( I ) , M )).

(3.4) The preceding lemma allows us to extend some parts of [3, Theorem 2.8] to modules which are not necessarily finitely generated.

Proposition 3.5. Let M be an R -module. If I and J are ideals of R such that √ I = √ J , then the following assertions are equivalent for any non-negative integer n .

- (1) Ext i R ( R/I,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .
- (2) Ext i R ( R/J,M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .
- (3) H i ( K ( I ) , M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .
- (4) H i ( K ( J ) , M ) ∈ S for 0 ⩽ i ⩽ n .
